name: Bassline
sources: style-research-extended vol.4 uk-garage — "4x4 / bassline: 135–142 BPM — 'most songs are around 135 to 142 bpm'. T2 'Heartbroken' 138–140"
style-research-extended vol.4 uk-garage — the 4x4/bassline variant: "revert to a straight four-on-the-floor kick and move all syncopation into the bassline"

style-research-extended vol.4 uk-garage — T2: straight 4x4 kick at 138–140, clap/snare on 2&4, 16th offbeat hats with moderate swing, tambourine; "the syncopation lives entirely in the bass, not the kit"; a low-frequency-oscillated warp/reese organ-bass playing a bouncing syncopated 16th figure that sits between the kicks, short, staccato, heavily filtered
style-research-extended vol.4 uk-garage — Bad Boy Chiller Crew: 130–140, 4x4 kick, clap on 2&4, offbeat open hat, 16th shaker; "treat swing as a per-record 50–65% variable rather than fixed"
style-research-extended-4 vol.4 header — `bassline` named among the archetypes that do not exist in this app
notes: The northern 4x4 wing that beat London 2-step to the chart, and the one archetype on this roster whose whole identity is **where the syncopation lives**. ⛔ **The sourced rule is a two-part swap: the kit goes straight and the bass takes the groove.** *"Revert to a straight four-on-the-floor kick and move all syncopation into the bassline"*, and *"the syncopation lives entirely in the bass, not the kit"*. So `kick.anchors` is all four quarters with `syncopation` at 0.08 — flatter than any other model here — while the low end runs a bouncing 16th figure between the kicks. ⛔⛔ **THE 808 LANE CANNOT PLAY BETWEEN THE KICKS, AND FINDING THAT OUT IS WHY THIS MODEL IS SHAPED THE WAY IT IS.** The first cut authored `bass808.role: "bassline"` with `kick.lockTo808` at 0.1, on the reasonable-sounding theory that an unlocked 808 would go its own way. It does not: `drums.rs` builds the 808 by *filtering the kick's own onsets* — `kicks.iter().filter(|_| rng.random_bool(lock))` — so a low lock makes the sub **sparser**, never syncopated. The invariant test measured 0% of the low end off the quarter and said so. ▶ **So the figure lives in the `bassline` block**, which is the only lane in this engine that places its own onsets: `rhythm: "independent_riff"` with a high `anticipationProb`, and `bass808.role` is `counter_riff` purely so `bass::generate` runs at all — it returns an empty lane whenever the 808 *is* the bassline. `kick.lockTo808` is 0.5 so the sub reinforces half the kicks rather than doubling all four, which is what a bassline record’s low end does under the organ. ⚠ **0.1 was the first value and a gate refused it**: `every_shipped_model_with_an_808_produces_a_playable_line` found seeds where the sub came out empty, and a model that authors an 808 has to play one. The syncopation was never in that lane anyway. ⚠ What the research calls a *"warp/reese organ-bass … short, staccato, heavily filtered"* is the `bassline` lane's register and `glideProb`; the sub underneath it is deliberately plain. ⚠ **Swing is a per-record variable and is authored at the middle of its range.** The research is explicit — *"some records import 'more highly swung beats instead of the classic 4x4 drums', so treat swing as a per-record 50–65% variable rather than fixed"* — and this engine authors one number per model, so 0.56 is the centre of that range rather than a claim that every bassline record swings the same. The `swung` mode reaches the top of it. ⚠ **Harmony is a two-bar organ loop and nothing more**: *"sampled Korg M1-style organ leads … usually a i–VI–VII or i–VII–VI loop of 2 bars"*, with flat minors dominating the modern wing (D♭m, A♭m, B♭m, F♯m) and major-key exceptions on the poppier singles. Both are in `keys`, weighted to the minors. ⚠ **INFERRED, hence `medium`.** Sourced: both tempo bands, the four-on-the-floor, the backbeat, the offbeat hats and shaker, the tambourine, the swing range, the organ harmony and its two-bar loop, the bass's shape and its placement between the kicks. Inferred: every velocity tier, every register, the `intervals`/`contour` split, the fill vocabulary and the mode names.
